object_description: long building with an open two-storey base and three teaching floors
design_condition: The building runs along the main street, is set back to widen the sidewalk and passage, places sports halls at its ends, and forms a large, publicly usable courtyard connected to an upper terrace.

positive.statement: The simple building figure respects the surrounding existing buildings to a high degree.
The arrangement creates the greatest possible open space between the neighboring buildings and the new building.
The passage, courtyard and sports-hall arrangement produces a strong openness toward the urban space.
The courtyard is well integrated into the neighborhood and supports dual use by the school and public.
The clear building structure and construction with supports and panels create a high level of flexibility.
The suspended platform creates spatial richness and sequences that merge without corridors.
The large terrace connects to the courtyard and adds an unusual spatial opportunity.
The covered access areas and courtyard-side lounge are attractive and work well in school operations.
The teaching floors are well lit, clear and furnished with well-proportioned classrooms.
The special classrooms are prominently arranged and positively enliven the street space.
The spatial program is implemented efficiently.
Daylight use is good and the ventilation principle is conceptually sensible.
The separated usage units enable a solid structural fire-protection concept.
The diverse entrances and exits support an open and communicative institution.

negative.statement: The scarce core areas inadequately meet the requirements for sanitary and service spaces.
The structural concept has weaknesses because some facade supports are not directly supported by the framework.
The rigid ceiling-to-facade connections are not convincing because of temperature deformation and thermal requirements.
The earthquake bracing still needs to be checked in the longitudinal direction.
The high gray energy per square meter results from the lack of compactness and complex supporting concept.
The external supporting facade is cost-intensive and challenging in terms of building physics.
The facade has not yet been mastered structurally and physically.
The above-average envelope and window proportions increase the technical and economic demands.
